edits.old: Analytics nodes add to the bill; prorating is not a promise of lower total spend. Studio 3T identifies workload-isolated analytics nodes as optional costs, and MongoDB's announcement describes them as additional read-only nodes. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Analytics nodes are an optional cost: Studio 3T lists workload-isolated analytics nodes among the optional costs of an Atlas cluster. MongoDB's Atlas documentation describes analytics nodes as nodes used to isolate analytical queries from the operational workload, and they can be sized on a different cluster tier than the operational nodes. Sources: https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/mongodb-atlas/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/workload-isolation/

evidence.quote: These optional costs include Atlas Search and Atlas Data Lake usage, multi-cloud configurations, global cluster configuration, multiple electable, read-only and workload-isolated analytics nodes.
Use analytics nodes to isolate queries which you do not wish to contend with your operational workload.
You can select a cluster tier for your analytics nodes that's larger or smaller than the cluster tier selected for your electable and read-only nodes (operational nodes).

edits.rationale: Studio 3T lists workload-isolated analytics nodes among optional Atlas costs, which supports the point that they add to the bill. The Atlas workload isolation docs describe analytics nodes as extra nodes that isolate analytical queries and can use their own tier. I found no source that says prorating does or does not lower total spend, and no MongoDB announcement describing analytics nodes as additional read-only nodes. Those two parts are left out.
